rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir reads singular here and in al-Maʿārij; the others read plural, which al-Samīn says better fits the intended generality.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير هنا وفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amāna is originally a verbal noun, but it can also denote the entrusted thing itself, as in the cited verses.
rows.anchor: الأمانة في الأصل مصدر، ويطلق على الشيء

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī argues that the commands to return and not betray trusts concern entrusted objects, since objects rather than abstract meanings are returned or betrayed.
rows.anchor: إنما يؤدى ويخان الأعيان لا المعاني، كذا قال الزمخشري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Samīn accepts al-Zamakhsharī's point about those two verses but says this verse can mean either the abstract trust or the entrusted object.
rows.anchor: أما ما ذكره من الآيتين فمسلم

rows.speaker: الأخوان
rows.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read the prayer term singular; the others use plural. Al-Samīn says al-Maʿārij has no disagreement on this point.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأخوان " على صلاتهم " بالتوحيد

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the first mention describes humility in prayer and the last its preservation, so the two mentions are not redundant.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " فإن قلت: كيف كرر ذكر الصلاة أولا وآخرا؟ قلت: هما ذكران مختلفان

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the first singular denotes prayer in general, while the final plural denotes preserving the five prayers, witr, and regular sunnas.
rows.anchor: ثم قال: " وأيضا فقد وحدت أولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Samīn says al-Zamakhsharī's explanation works only for readings other than those of the two readers, who use singular at both places; al-Zamakhsharī also reported disagreement on the second form.
rows.anchor: قلت: وهذا إنما يتجه في قراءة غير الأخوين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If mā is a relative pronoun, the object pronoun is omitted; the deletion meets the conditions because preposition and governor match, no nominative is displaced, and no other pronoun remains.
rows.anchor: هذا إذا جعلناها بمعنى الذي فإن جعلتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If mā is a verbal noun, it needs no resumptive pronoun, and the verbal noun occupies the object position, meaning what they drink.
rows.anchor: فإن جعلتها مصدرا لم تحتج إلى عائد

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ is reported as construing the phrase with an omitted min, as though it said they drink from it; al-Samīn says this extra preposition is unnecessary.
rows.anchor: وزعم الفراء أن معنى " ما تشربون " على حذف أي:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Samīn rejects the claim that this deletion is barred for Basran grammarians: the conditions are met, though omitting min from the relative construction loses the partitive parallel with what they eat.
rows.anchor: يعني أنه يقدر: تشربونه من غير حرف جر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: First analysis: the first anna has an omitted noun annexed to the address pronoun, with that pronoun standing in its place; its predicate is the if-clause, and the second anna repeats it to clarify the omission.
rows.anchor: مضاف لضمير الخطاب حذف وأقيم المضاف إليه مقامه

rows.speaker: الجرمي والمبرد والفراء
rows.claim: The second analysis makes makhrajūn the predicate of the first anna and governor of idhā; the second anna repeats the first after a long separation.
rows.anchor: وإليه ذهب الجرمي والمبرد والفراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Third analysis: the second anna-clause is a nominative verbal noun; an omitted verb is the conditional answer to idhā, and that answer plus the if-clause predicates the first anna.
rows.anchor: ذلك الفعل المحذوف هو جواب " إذا " الشرطية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fourth analysis also treats the second anna-clause as a verbal noun raised by an omitted verb, but that verb itself predicates the first anna and governs idhā.
rows.anchor: إلا أن هذا الفعل المقدر خبر ل " أن " الأولى

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sībawayh omits the first anna's predicate, estimated as your resurrection; it governs the time phrase, and the second anna-clause is an apposition to the first.
rows.anchor: بدل من الأولى، وهذا مذهب سيبويه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sixth analysis treats the second anna-clause as a subject with the time phrase as its fronted predicate; the whole clause predicates the first anna.
rows.anchor: أن { أنكم مخرجون } مبتدأ، وخبره الظرف مقدما عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Makhrajūn cannot govern idhā, because material governed by anna cannot govern material before it; mat tum also cannot govern it because it is genitive as the complement of muḍāf.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يكون العامل في " إذا " " مخرجون " على كل قول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The anna-clause is accusative or genitive after omission of its original preposition, though Arabic also permits it without a preposition in the accusative.
rows.anchor: و " أنكم " وما في حيزه في محل نصب أو جر بعد حذف الحرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun hī is explained by context: the intended sense is that their life is only this worldly life.
rows.anchor: " هي " ضمير يفسره سياق الكلام

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the pronoun's referent is only known from what follows; the original was al-ḥayātu, replaced by hī because the predicate identifies it.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " هذا ضمير لا يعلم ما يراد به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Samīn says classifying this as a phrase explained by what follows in both wording and syntax does not apply to al-Zamakhsharī's quoted explanation, despite an attribution to him.
rows.anchor: إلى الزمخشري متعلقا بهذا الكلام الذي نقلته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause explains the claim that their life consists only of this cycle.
rows.anchor: جملة مفسرة لما ادعوه من أن حياتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Samīn rejects using the verb order to prove that wāw does not imply sequence: apparently some die and others live successively, each generation replacing another.
rows.anchor: الظاهر من معناها: يموت البعض منا، ويحيا آخرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation is that the speakers mean that they themselves die while their children live on.
rows.anchor: وقيل: نموت نحن ويحيا أبناؤنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that they believe in return to life: they die, then live again after that death.
rows.anchor: وقيل: القوم يعتقدون الرجعة أي: نموت ثم نحيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghuthāʾ is the second object of jaʿala, which here means to turn them into something.
rows.anchor: مفعول ثان للجعل بمعنى التصيير

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash glosses ghuthāʾ as jifāʾ, flood-scum or debris; al-Samīn notes the word earlier in al-Raʿd.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم في الرعد. قاله الأخفش

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj defines it as decayed leaves that mix with foam when a flood runs.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: " هو البالي من ورق الشجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another gloss is anything useless carried off by a flood or left in a cooking pot; it became proverbial for worthless remains.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كل ما يلقيه السيل والقدر مما لا ينتفع به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ghuthāʾ the final root radical is wāw, as in ghaṯā al-wādī; the similar nausea verb ghathiyat is from the yāʾ root and is close in sense.
rows.anchor: ولامه واو لأنه من غثا الوادي يغثو غثوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word is pronounced with either doubled or light thāʾ; its plural aghthāʾ is irregular, since the expected forms would be aghthiya or ghithyān.
rows.anchor: وتشدد ثاء " الغثاء " وتخفف وقد جمع على " أغثاء "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Samīn cites an Imruʾ al-Qays line using ghuthāʾ alongside flood debris as poetic evidence for the word.
rows.anchor: من السيل والغثاء فلكة مغزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Buʿdan is a verbal noun in place of its verb and must be governed by an implicit verb because it expresses a curse or prayer against them.
rows.anchor: بعدا: مصدر بدل من اللفظ بفعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source gives both baʿuda buʿdan and baʿida baʿdan, by analogy with the two forms of rashada rushdan.
rows.anchor: والأصل: بعد بعدا وبعدا نحو: رشد رشدا ورشدا

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes the lām as attached to an omitted explanatory phrase, as in suqyā lahu and jadʿan lahu.
rows.anchor: كهي في سقيا له وجدعا له. قاله الزمخشري

rows.speaker: الحوفي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥawfī attaches the lām to buʿdan, but al-Samīn rejects this as unattested.
rows.anchor: قاله الحوفي. وهذا مردود؛/ لأنه لا يحفظ حذف هذه اللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In fa-taʿsan lahum, the lām also attaches to an omitted phrase rather than to taʿsan, so it cannot support direct attachment here.
rows.anchor: ولذلك منعوا الاشتغال في قوله والذين كفروا فتعسا لهم

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read the wāw with kasra to break the meeting of two vowelless letters.
rows.anchor: الجمهور على كسر الواو لالتقاء الساكنين

rows.speaker: ابن وثاب
rows.claim: Ibn Waththāb reads the wāw with ḍamma, by analogy with the pronoun wāw, whose kasra was itself analogized to this wāw.
rows.anchor: وابن وثاب بضمها تشبيها بواو الضمير كما كسرت واو الضمير تشبيها بها

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The common reading uses the first-person plural, with God as speaker; the intended sense is that His messengers brought them the reminder.
rows.anchor: العامة على إسناد الفعل إلى ضمير المتكلم المعظم نفسه

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr has a long vowel in ātaynāhum, meaning we gave them; its second object may be omitted or may be bidhikrihim, with the bāʾ extra.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو في رواية " آتيناهم " بالمد بمعنى أعطيناهم

rows.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق وعيسى بن عمر وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: These readers also have ataytuhum with first-person singular tāʾ.
rows.anchor: وابن أبي إسحاق وعيسى بن عمر وأبو عمرو أيضا " أتيتهم "

rows.speaker: أبو البرهسم وأبو حيوة والجحدري وأبو رجاء
rows.claim: These readers use second-person singular tāʾ, addressing the Messenger.
rows.anchor: وأبو البرهسم وأبو حيوة والجحدري وأبو رجاء " أتيتهم "

rows.speaker: عيسى
rows.claim: ʿĪsā reads bidhikrāhum, with the feminine long ā.
rows.anchor: وعيسى " بذكراهم " بألف التأنيث

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda reads nudhakkiruhum, a first-person plural imperfect of the intensive verb; it forms a circumstantial clause in place of the prepositional phrase.
rows.anchor: وقتادة " نذكرهم " بنون المتكلم المعظم نفسه مكان باء الجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Samīn notes that the kharj and kharāj discussion was treated earlier in al-Kahf.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم الكلام في " خرجا " و " خراج " في الكهف

rows.speaker: الأخوان
rows.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read shaqāwatanā with fatḥa on shīn and a long ā after qāf; others have shaqwatanā with kasra on shīn and vowelless qāf.
rows.anchor: قرأ الأخوان: " شقاوتنا " بفتح الشين وألف بعد القاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forms are verbal nouns with the same meaning; shaqāwa resembles qasāwa and is widespread, while shaqwa resembles fiṭna and niʿma and is Hijazi.
rows.anchor: وهما مصدران بمعنى واحد، فالشقاوة كالقساوة

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ cites a line with shaqwatihi as evidence for the Hijazi form.
rows.anchor: والشقوة كالفطنة والنعمة. وأنشد الفراء:

rows.speaker: قتادة والحسن
rows.claim: Qatāda and al-Ḥasan in one transmission match the two readers' long-vowel form but use kasra on shīn.
rows.anchor: قرأ قتادة والحسن في رواية كالأخوين إلا أنهما

rows.speaker: شبل
rows.claim: Shibl's preferred reading matches the majority's short form but has fatḥa on shīn.
rows.anchor: وشبل في اختياره كالباقين، إلا أنه فتح الشين

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ begins with parsing the pronoun as the pronoun of the matter.
rows.anchor: أحدها: أنها ضمير الشأن. وبه بدأ أبو البقاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second parse makes the pronoun refer to Satan.
rows.anchor: والثاني: أنها ضمير الشيطان. وهذان الوجهان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third parse makes the pronoun return to the conditional relative man, whoever follows Satan.
rows.anchor: والثالث: أنه عائد على " من " الشرطية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The matter-pronoun and Satan-reference parses are valid only for grammarians who do not require the conditional noun to have a resumptive pronoun in the answer clause.
rows.anchor: وهذان الوجهان إنما يجوزان على رأي من لا يشترط

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read the kāf lightly, from zakā yazkū; its final alif is read with or without imāla.
rows.anchor: العامة على تخفيف الكاف يقال: زكا يزكو

rows.speaker: الأعمش وأبو جعفر
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash and Abū Jaʿfar read the kāf doubled. The alif is written as yāʾ unusually, either reflecting imāla or spelling the doubled reading.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش وأبو جعفر بتشديدها. وكتبت ألفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the light reading, min aḥadin is the subject; with the doubled reading it is the object. Min is extra in either parse, and God is the subject in both.
rows.anchor: فعلى قراءة التخفيف يكون " من أحد " فاعلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: First parse: fī buyūt is an adjective of the niche, meaning a niche in a house of God.
rows.anchor: أحدها: أنها صفة ل " مشكاة " أي: كمشكاة في بيوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Second parse makes fī buyūt an adjective of the lamp.
rows.anchor: الثاني: أنه صفة لمصباح. الثالث:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Third parse makes fī buyūt an adjective of the glass.
rows.anchor: الثالث: أنه صفة ل " زجاجة "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fourth parse attaches it to tūqadu; the first four parses do not allow a pause at ʿalīm.
rows.anchor: الرابع: أنه متعلق ب " توقد ". وعلى هذه الأقوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fifth parse connects the phrase to an omitted verb, as in the phrase about nine signs: He is glorified in houses; this allows pausing at ʿalīm.
rows.anchor: الخامس: أنه متعلق بمحذوف كقوله في تسع آيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sixth parse attaches it to yusabbiḥ, so men glorify God in houses; the repeated fīhā is emphatic, as in the cited verse, and a pause at ʿalīm is possible.
rows.anchor: وفيها تكرير للتوكيد كقوله: ففي الجنة خالدين فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Samīn notes that al-Shaykh says there are three such parses but actually names only two.
rows.anchor: وقال الشيخ: " وعلى هذه الأقوال الثلاثة " ولم يذكر سوى قولين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause with adhina Allāh is an adjective of buyūt; an is preceded by an omitted preposition, as though it said fī an turfaʿ.
rows.anchor: في محل جر صفة ل " بيوت "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fī buyūt cannot attach to yudhkar, because that verb is coordinated inside the complement of an, and material after an cannot be moved before it.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز تعلق " في بيوت " بقوله: " ويذكر "

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وأبو بكر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Bakr read yusabbaḥu with fatḥa on bāʾ, in the passive; one of the three genitive phrases becomes deputy subject, with the first preferred because the verb needs a nominative and it is nearer.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر وأبو بكر بفتح الباء مبنيا للمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the passive reading, rijāl may be nominative after an omitted verb answering an implied question, Who glorifies Him? Al-Samīn cites a poetic line with ḍāriʿ as such an answer, while noting disagreement over this construction.
rows.anchor: كأنه قيل: من يبكيه؟ فقيل: يبكيه ضارع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second parse makes rijāl the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning those who glorify Him are men; this reading allows a pause at al-āṣāl.
rows.anchor: والوجه الثاني في البيت: أن " يزيد " منادى

rows.speaker: باقي السبعة
rows.claim: The other canonical readers use active yusabbiḥu with kasra on bāʾ, making rijāl the subject; there is then no pause at al-āṣāl.
rows.anchor: وباقي السبعة بكسر الباء مبنيا للفاعل. والفاعل " رجال "

rows.speaker: ابن وثاب وأبو حيوة
rows.claim: Ibn Waththāb and Abū Ḥaywa read tusabbiḥu with feminine tāʾ and active kasra, since a broken plural can take feminine agreement.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن وثاب وأبو حيوة " تسبح " بالتاء من فوق

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar uses the same feminine tāʾ but passive fatḥa; al-Zamakhsharī parses the times as subject with an extra bāʾ, while others make glorification the implied deputy subject, figuratively attributed to those times.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر كذلك إلا أنه فتح الباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Samīn prefers the implied tasbīḥa as deputy subject: glorification is metaphorically attributed to morning and evening, and this fits better than the cited al-Jāthiya example because no explicit object occurs here.
rows.anchor: وخرجها غيره على أن القائم مقام الفاعل ضمير التسبيحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The al-Jāthiya reading is parsed as an implied al-jazāʾ, the recompense, being given to a people.
rows.anchor: كما خرجوا قراءة أبي جعفر أيضا { ليجزى قوما بما كانوا يكسبون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause lā tulhīhim is a nominative adjective describing rijāl.
rows.anchor: في محل رفع صفة ل " رجال "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yakhāfūn may be a second adjective of rijāl or a circumstantial clause describing the object of tulhīhim.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن تكون نعتا ثانيا لرجال، وأن تكون حالا من مفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the stronger parse, yawman is a direct object rather than an adverb, and yataqallabu is an adjective of that day.
rows.anchor: و " يوما " مفعول به لا ظرف على الأظهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative alladhī may be nominative as an adjective of the preceding alladhī.
rows.anchor: يجوز في " الذي " الرفع نعتا للذي الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the relative may be nominative as an explanatory apposition to the preceding alladhī.
rows.anchor: أو بيانا، أو بدلا، أو خبرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it may be the predicate of an omitted subject.
rows.anchor: أو بدلا، أو خبرا لمبتدأ محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A final option is accusative case as a laudatory construction.
rows.anchor: أو النصب على المدح. وما بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The material after nazala still belongs to the first relative clause, so it is not an intervening foreign clause and does not disrupt attachment of the second relative as its dependent.
rows.anchor: وما بعد " نزل " من تمام الصلة فليس أجنبيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here khalq means bringing into being and preparing each thing for its proper function, allowing fa-qaddarahu to add that He determined it precisely; taking khalq as determination would make the wording redundant.
rows.anchor: الخلق هنا عبارة عن الإحداث والتهيئة لما يصلح له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jumlata is a circumstantial accusative describing the Qurʾān, with the sense of its being brought down all together.
rows.anchor: حال من القرآن، إذ هي في معنى مجتمعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parse puts kathālika in a nominative position: the matter is so; li-nuthabbita then gives the reason for an omitted verb, we did that to strengthen your heart.
rows.anchor: إما مرفوعة المحل أي: الأمر كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively kathālika is a circumstantial accusative meaning it was sent down in that manner, or it qualifies an omitted verbal noun; li-nuthabbita attaches to that omitted verb.
rows.anchor: وإما منصوبته على الحال أي: أنزل مثل ذلك

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: Abū Ḥātim calls kathālika the answer to an oath; al-Samīn judges this weak and says al-Akhfash took that approach for wa-li-taṣghā as well.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حاتم: " هي جواب قسم " وهذا قول مرجوح

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh reads liyuthbita with yāʾ, making God the subject.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله " ليثبت " بالياء أي: الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tartīl means separating or spacing things out, including the succession of one word after another with a slight pause but no break in breath.
rows.anchor: والترتيل: التفريق. ومجيء الكلمة بعد الأخرى بسكون يسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word ratal for teeth describes slight spaces between them, as in thaghr ratil or murattal.
rows.anchor: ومنه ثغر رتل ومرتل أي: مفلج الأسنان

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes nuzzila here to mean anzala, without an implication of gradual revelation, to avoid conflict with the demand that the Qurʾān come all at once.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " ونزل هنا بمعنى: أنزل لا غير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Samīn says al-Zamakhsharī's argument assumes the intensive pattern signals distribution or gradualness; earlier discussions and an Ibn ʿAbbās report seem to support this on the surface.
rows.anchor: وهذا بناء منه على معتقده وهو أن التضعيف يدل على التفريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An ellipsis is required: either they hear your invocation, making the verb take one object, or they hear you invoking, making it take two; al-Fārisī treats the supplied clause as the second object, while others make it circumstantial.
rows.anchor: لا بد من محذوف أي: يسمعون دعاءكم، أو يسمعونكم تدعون

rows.speaker: قتادة ويحيى بن يعمر
rows.claim: Qatāda and Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar read yusmiʿūnakum with ḍamma on yāʾ and kasra on mīm; the second object is omitted, meaning they make you hear the answer.
rows.anchor: وقرأ قتادة ويحيى بن يعمر بضم الياء وكسر الميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idh is governed by the preceding verb; both verbs are past in meaning despite future forms, since the first governs idh and idh governs the second.
rows.anchor: { إذ تدعون } منصوب بما قبله، فما قبله وما بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some grammarians take idh here to mean idhā, when.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: " إذ " هنا بمعنى إذا

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī reads it as a vivid recollection of past circumstances, telling the idolaters to recall their invocations and answer whether the idols heard them; this sharpens the rebuke.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: " إنه على حكاية الحال الماضية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prior discussion noted readings that assimilate the dhāl of idh into tāʾ or pronounce it distinctly.
rows.anchor: وإظهارها في التاء. وقال ابن عطية

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya suggests applying the assimilation analogy of words like mudakkir here; it would yield a doubled dāl followed by a vowelless dāl.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: ويجوز فيه قياس " مدكر " ونحوه

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: Al-Shaykh rejects Ibn ʿAṭiyya's analogy: assimilation applies to the infix tāʾ in specified derived forms or a pronoun suffix, not the imperfect prefix tāʾ.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وهذا لا يجوز؛ لأن هذا الإبدال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kathālika is accusative, governed by yafʿalūn, with the sense they do the same as we do; yafʿalūn is the second object of wajadnā.
rows.anchor: يفعلون في محل نصب مفعولا ثانيا ل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in wa-innahu refers to the Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: أي: وإن القرآن. وقيل: وإن محمدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes the pronoun to refer to Muḥammad.
rows.anchor: وقيل: وإن محمدا. وفيه التفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording shifts person: continuation of the preceding direct address would have said wa-innaka, you are in the earlier scriptures.
rows.anchor: وفيه التفات؛ إذ لو جرى على ما تقدم

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads zubur with a vowelless bāʾ, a lightened form of the standard reading.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش " زبر " بسكون الباء

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads takun with feminine tāʾ and āyatun in the nominative.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر " تكن " بالتاء من فوق " آية " بالرفع

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The other readers use masculine yakun and āyatan in the accusative.
rows.anchor: والباقون " يكن " بالياء من تحت " آية " بالنصب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reads feminine takun with āyatan in the accusative.
rows.anchor: وابن عباس " تكن " بالتاء من فوق و " آية " بالنصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For Ibn ʿĀmir's reading, takūnu may be a complete verb: lahum attaches to it and āya is its subject; an yaʿlamahu is either apposition to āya or a predicate of an omitted subject.
rows.anchor: فأما قراءة ابن عامر ف " تكون " تحتمل أن تكون تامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On an incomplete-verb parse, one option makes the subject the pronoun of the matter and the following clause its predicate.
rows.anchor: أحدها: أن يكون اسمها مضمرا فيها بمعنى القصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second incomplete parse makes the matter-pronoun its subject, lahum its fronted predicate, and āya its delayed subject; an yaʿlamahu is apposition or a predicate of an omitted subject.
rows.anchor: الثاني: أن يكون اسمها ضمير القصة أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third incomplete parse makes lahum the fronted predicate of takun and āya its subject; an yaʿlamahu is again apposition or a predicate of an omitted subject.
rows.anchor: الثالث: أن يكون " لهم " خبر " تكن " مقدما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth parse makes āya the subject and an yaʿlamahu its predicate, but objections call the indefinite subject before a definite predicate poetic necessity; al-Samīn rejects that defense and says there is no need for this parse.
rows.anchor: ولا ضرورة تدعو إلى هذا التخريج، بل التخريج ما تقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the other readers, āyatan is a fronted predicate, an yaʿlamahu the delayed subject, and lahum attaches circumstantially to āya.
rows.anchor: وأما قراءة الباقين فواضحة جدا ف " آية " خبر مقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās's agreement pattern parallels the cited verse and poetry: a feminine verb can agree with a feminine predicate or a verbal noun understood as feminine.
rows.anchor: وأما قراءة ابن عباس فكقراءة { ثم لم تكن فتنتهم إلا أن قالوا }

rows.speaker: الجحدري
rows.claim: Al-Jaḥdarī reads an taʿlamahu with feminine tāʾ, treating Banū Isrāʾīl, a broken plural, as a feminine singular for agreement.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجحدري: " أن تعلمه " بالتاء من فوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited line uses feminine singular qālat with the tribe name Banū ʿĀmir, providing a poetic parallel for the agreement.
rows.anchor: قالت بنو عامر خالوا بني أسد يا بؤس للجهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The written rasm has a wāw after the mīm plus alif; one explanation is a dialect that inclines alif toward wāw, as in ṣalāh and zakāh.
rows.anchor: وكتبوا في الرسم الكريم " علمؤا " بواو الميم والألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idh qāla may be governed by an omitted remember or know, inferred from ʿalīm or ḥalīm; al-Samīn finds this weak because it binds the attribute to this circumstance.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون منصوبا بإضمار اذكر أو تعلم مقدرا

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: The Kufans use nunation on shihāb, parsing qabas either as an appositive or as an adjective meaning something taken as a firebrand.
rows.anchor: قرأ الكوفيون بتنوين " شهاب " على أن قبسا بدل

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The other readers use genitive annexation as an explanatory relation, since a shihāb may be a firebrand or something else.
rows.anchor: والباقون بالإضافة على البيان؛ لأن الشهاب يكون قبسا وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A shihāb is a flame, while a qabas is a piece of it, whether or not it is on a stick.
rows.anchor: والشهاب: الشعلة. والقبس: القطعة منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aw has its ordinary sense of offering alternatives of different kinds.
rows.anchor: على بابها من التنويع. والطاء في

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ṭāʾ in taṣṭalūn replaces the tāʾ of the iftiʿāl form, from ṣaliya bi-l-nār.
rows.anchor: والطاء في " تصطلون " بدل من تاء الافتعال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wajadtu-hā means I encountered or found her and takes one object; yasjudūn and its coordinated material are circumstantial clauses describing that object.
rows.anchor: فتتعدى لواحد، فيكون " يسجدون " حالا من مفعولها

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī reads the first word lightly: it is an attention particle, followed by yāʾ as attention or address, then the imperative; the written form joins the particles because their alif and hamza are not pronounced, so both readings coincide in sound and script but differ in analysis.
rows.anchor: فقد عرفت أن قراءة الكسائي قوية لكثرة دورها في لغتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Samīn prefers yāʾ as an attention particle over an elided vocative to avoid excessive deletion; although alā precedes it, paired particles are defensible for emphasis, as Arabic usage attests.
rows.anchor: سمع بعضهم يقول: ألا يا ارحموني، ألا يا تصدقوا علينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Several poems by unnamed poets use alā yā before imperatives such as اسلمي, اسقياني, and اسمع; prose likewise has alā yā arḥamūnī and alā yā taṣaddaqū.
rows.anchor: سمع بعضهم يقول: ألا يا ارحموني، ألا يا تصدقوا علينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further line has yā before a command without preceding alā; in a line about God's curse, yā may be vocative with an omitted addressee, though attention is preferred.
rows.anchor: يا دار هند يا اسلمي ثم اسلمي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī allows a full stop at yahtadūn, or test stops at alā yā, alā alone, or yā alone; the latter are not chosen stops because the particles need what follows to complete their sense.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن الكسائي الوقف عنده على " يهتدون " تام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the other readers, one parse expands allā to an lā: an governs the subjunctive, lā is extra, and the phrase is the object of yahtadūn after an omitted preposition, meaning toward not prostrating; al-Samīn cites the parallel liallâ yaʿlama.
rows.anchor: أصلها: أن لا، ف " أن " ناصبة للفعل بعدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second parse makes the phrase an appositive to aʿmālahum, with a parenthetical interruption: Satan beautified their failure to prostrate to God.
rows.anchor: الثاني: أنه بدل من " أعمالهم " وما بينهما اعتراض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third parse makes it an appositive to al-sabīl, with an extra lā, meaning Satan turned them away from prostrating to God.
rows.anchor: الثالث: أنه بدل من " السبيل " على زيادة " لا "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth analysis treats the phrase as a purpose accusative attached either to zayyana or ṣaddahum; lā may be ordinary negation or extra.
rows.anchor: الرابع: أن { ألا يسجدوا } مفعول له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With lā non-extra, Satan beautified or diverted them so they would not prostrate; if extra, it means he did so expecting or fearing their prostration.
rows.anchor: وفي " لا " حينئذ وجهان، أحدهما: أنه ليست مزيدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Samīn prefers treating lā in the purpose-accusative parse as non-extra.
rows.anchor: لأجل خوفه من سجودهم. وعدم الزيادة أظهر
